author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island’s peak fall color may arrive later than usual this year, with a warmer growing season potentially pushing the best viewing into early November. Storm Team 10 says the typical late-October peak across Rhode Island, southeastern Massachusetts and southern Connecticut could be delayed by one to two weeks.

The outlook is a forecast, not a fixed calendar. Leaf color and timing depend on temperatures, daylight, moisture and wind, and conditions can vary between inland and coastal locations. Above-average warmth can slow the seasonal changes that trigger leaves to turn, while a major windstorm can shorten the viewing window by stripping leaves early.

Forecasters said the region’s relatively calm summer and early fall may help leaves remain on branches. They also pointed to adequate precipitation after a dry spring as a factor that could support healthy color. Despite the possible delay, the forecast continues to call for vibrant foliage.

For visitors planning trips, the timing means flexibility may be more useful than relying on a single traditional peak weekend. Northern New England usually turns first, followed by central and southern areas. Residents should watch updated local foliage maps and short-range weather forecasts as October approaches, since a cold snap or strong coastal storm could still change the schedule.
dek: Forecasters say above-average warmth may push southern New England’s best color back one or two weeks, while calm conditions could help leaves stay on trees.
headline: Warmer season could delay Rhode Island peak foliage into November
